title: THE INTERPRETER WHO WAS ASKED TO SOFTEN THE WORD
deck: A blockading captain says a maybe will be taken as a yes. The harbourmaster's nineteen-year-old interpreter is ordered to render a flat refusal as 'we are considering it'. Illuminara has no standing at the table, so she sits behind him and waits for him to ask her a question.
shape: Six scenes across one night and the day after: an order to soften a word, a table where the exact refusal is spoken and read back, a quay where a ship says what it will allow and how a person may be asked, a harbourmaster made to say each concession aloud, a morning of read-backs and a staged, reversible trust, and the hour after the deadline passes quietly.

scenes.title: Two Words and Three More
paragraphs: *Council hall, Calder harbour · twenty-five hours before the deadline, 22:40*
The harbourmaster of Calder had written his answer on the back of a tide table, and it was two words long.

Quillan Abara laid it in front of Bram Ivarsson. Bram was nineteen. He had interpreted for fishwives and customs clerks, and never for anyone with a gun. Illuminara sat on a stacking chair against the wall, where the council had put her because nobody could say what else she was. Through the window the cruiser *Marin Resolute* lay across the harbour mouth like a shut door, every deck light burning.

**Quillan**  
Read it.

**Bram**  
No. We will not hand over the *Tamsin Reach*.

**Quillan**  
That is my answer, and it is the right one. Now hear what you will say at the table.
He took the tide table back and wrote three more words under the first two, pressing hard enough to dent the paper.

**Quillan**  
*We are considering it.* A captain who hears considering waits. A captain who hears no fires. Captain Vey has told us how he hears things, and I would rather not be heard.

**Bram**  
He said a maybe would be taken as a yes.

**Quillan**  
Then I will have a night before anyone finds out it was not. Sixty thousand people need a night, boy. You carry what you are given. That is the whole of the work.

Bram looked at the two words and the three. He had a good memory for what people said, and it was the only thing he was sure he was good at. *If I carry the three, I have put a lie in my own mouth and called it a favour.*

**Bram**  
I'll carry the no, Harbourmaster. I don't know that I can carry the other.

Quillan did not answer. He turned to the window and stood with his hands behind him, like a man waiting on a sentence he had already served. Illuminara said nothing. She had no standing in that room, and she had come to think the kindest thing she could be was a chair that did not lean.

scenes.title: What the Captain Would Hear
paragraphs: *Customs shed, Calder quay · 23:30*

Captain Anselm Vey had the stillness of a man who had not slept for two days and did not intend to mention it. He came ashore in the cruiser's launch with one aide, who wrote and never spoke, and he sat across the customs table with his cap squared in front of him.

**Vey**  
Harbourmaster. You have had the evening. What is your answer?
Quillan spoke in Harbourish, four short words. Bram turned to the captain. His voice came out smaller than he wanted, and he let it.

**Bram**  
The harbourmaster says no. We will not hand over the ship.
The aide's pen stopped. Vey looked at Bram for a long moment, and Illuminara, from her chair by the door, saw the captain take in that the young man had not said *considering*.

**Vey**  
Then I will tell you how I hear that. At midnight tomorrow my guns open on this quay. Nothing said after tonight reaches anyone who can stop them.

Bram rendered it. Quillan's jaw moved. Bram felt the room tilt toward the one thing he had not been told he could do, and asked for water. In the corridor he leaned on the wall, and Illuminara came out and stood at a distance he could close or not.

**Bram**  
I did it right. I said it exactly, and he will fire. I made it worse.

**Illuminara**  
What did he say he would do? Not what you heard. What he said.

**Bram**  
At midnight tomorrow he opens fire. Nothing said after tonight reaches anyone who can stop it.

**Illuminara**  
That is a date and a fear. It does not say what would change it. What would you want to know, if it were you who had to carry it back to a command?
He stared at her. Then, slowly, something in his face stopped bracing and started working.

**Bram**  
I'm allowed to read back. Everything I think I heard, before I answer. Nobody has ever asked me to use it on a captain.

**Illuminara**  
I won't tell you what to ask. I'll be here.
When he came back in, he did not sit. He said it in Marin first, then in Harbourish, slowly, so that both men heard what he had understood.

**Bram**  
Captain, I will say back what I heard, and you will tell me where I am wrong. At midnight tomorrow you fire. I understood that you fire unless a yes is given. Is that what you mean, or do you mean unless something is given that you can report?
Vey said nothing for several breaths. His aide had begun to write again.

**Vey**  
Not a yes. I do not need your ship. My command was told there are weapons aboard it and one man they want. I am ordered to fire unless I hold an answer to that claim that I can verify. A yes is verifiable. A maybe is not. A no with nothing behind it is not either.

**Bram**  
That is two claims, Captain, and the harbourmaster will answer them separately. Weapons, and a man. What is the claim about the man?

**Vey**  
A warrant from the Eastern court of the Concord. Teodor Lask, accused of burning a grain store at Orrin Ford. I have no evidence beyond the paper. I do not know that he is aboard. My command says he is. I am not a court, and I am not asking you to be one.

**Bram**  
Then what would you accept as an answer about him?

**Vey**  
That someone who answers to no navy looked, and wrote what he found, and that I can sign my name under what he wrote. I cannot sign under a refusal.
Bram rendered all of it to Quillan, every word, and watched the harbourmaster hear for the first time what the door was made of.

**Bram**  
Harbourmaster, the captain can live with a no if it comes with a way to answer his claim. I cannot offer one. An interpreter does not add.

**Quillan**  
I will not have Concord boots on a refugee deck. And I will not hand over a man on a captain's paper.

**Bram**  
That is two refusals. I do not yet know what else is yours to open.

**Quillan**  
Not at the table. Not under guns. I will answer at four.
Vey allowed it. His aide drew a line under the page.

scenes.title: What the Ship Would Allow
paragraphs: *Quay, beside the Tamsin Reach · 01:20*

The ship was a coastal packet built for ninety and carrying two hundred and twelve. Sefa Harrow, a retired schoolteacher with a blanket over her shoulders and a clipboard she no longer needed, met Illuminara at the foot of the gangway and did not offer her a hand.

**Sefa**  
Everybody wants to speak for us tonight. The harbourmaster, the captain, the radio. You are the first person to come down here and ask.

**Illuminara**  
I haven't asked yet. I came to ask what you would never allow. Then what you could.

**Sefa**  
Names. A list of two hundred and twelve names in a Concord office is two hundred and twelve people they can find. Not one name leaves this ship.

**Illuminara**  
Then no names. What else?

**Sefa**  
Forty-one of mine are sick. Some have been sick for a week. Whatever anyone wants to see in my hold, let them see the sick walk off first.
A child coughed somewhere above them, a hard wet cough. Sefa waited until it had passed.

**Sefa**  
And you should hear this from me before you hear it from a captain. There are two crates of hunting rifles in the hold. Two families brought them from the coast out of habit. He is not wholly wrong, and I will not lie to anyone you send.

**Illuminara**  
Then you say it yourself, to whoever looks. I will not tell it for you. There is one more thing in his claim, and it is not cargo. A man. Do you want the name, or only that there is one?

**Sefa**  
Say it. Hearing is not giving.

**Illuminara**  
Teodor Lask. A warrant from the Eastern court, for burning a grain store at Orrin Ford. The captain says he does not know whether the man is aboard.
Sefa's face did not change. Somewhere above them a cough stopped, or a breath did. Illuminara could not have said which, and did not look up.

**Sefa**  
I will not tell you whether I know that name. If I say no, I owe a captain the proof of a no. If I say yes, I have handed him a man because a navy put a paper in front of me. Neither answer leaves this ship.

**Illuminara**  
Then what can?

**Sefa**  
A vote cannot give away a person. It can only decide how he is asked. So: someone who answers to no navy puts one question to every adult aboard, alone. Are you the man in this paper? Each answers for themselves and nobody for anyone else. It is written down, sealed and kept by that neutral until a hearing on land, with counsel for whoever stands in it. The captain may have the fact that the question was asked of all of us. He may not have an answer.

**Illuminara**  
I will carry exactly that, and nothing beside it.

**Sefa**  
We vote at three. By hand, in the hold, every one of us over twelve. I will tell you at four what the ship says.

At ten to four she came to the gangway alone. The ship had voted. The rifles would be sealed and held by a neutral inspector until the harbour was safe. The sick would go first. The question would be put to every adult alone, and no answer would leave the ship. No name would leave the ship. One man had voted against and was not speaking to anyone, and Sefa said so without apology.

scenes.title: Say It Aloud
paragraphs: *Council hall, Calder harbour · 04:20*
Quillan was still in his coat. Bram had brought tea and put it down without being thanked, and then he did something that cost him: he did not sit.

**Bram**  
Harbourmaster, I will carry your no at eight exactly as you gave it. I won't say considering. If you order it, I will tell you now that I won't, and you can send for someone else.

**Quillan**  
You are nineteen.

**Bram**  
Yes. The captain fires at midnight on a no with nothing in it. I will not be the mouth that says you were thinking when you were not. Tell me what is yours to open. Say each thing aloud, and I will say it back to you, and then I will carry exactly that and nothing more.
Illuminara stood by the door. Sefa had asked her to carry the ship's four conditions to him, and she had done so in the hall at four, word for word. She added nothing now.

**Quillan**  
A neutral inspector. Not Concord's man. Tomas Brightwater of the Lantern Mission has waited in the town since the first day.

**Bram**  
A neutral inspector, Brightwater of the Lantern Mission, not a Concord officer. Is that yours to give?

**Quillan**  
It is. The sick, first, at nine, onto my quay, into my ambulances. And if the guns move back, a talk at dawn the day after.

**Bram**  
The sick landed at nine, by your ambulances. If the guns move back, a talk at dawn the day after. Is that yours to give?

**Quillan**  
It is. And the ship's fourth condition, the question put to each adult alone. My harbour allows Brightwater to ask it, on my quay and in their hold. The answers are theirs. I will not be heard promising a navy what is not mine to promise.

**Bram**  
The harbour allows the question to be asked. The answers belong to the ship. Is that what you give?

**Quillan**  
That is exactly what I give. And hear this, because I will not have it said later that I chose it gladly. I am doing this because a boy would not lie for me.

**Bram**  
I'll render that as well, if you wish.

**Quillan**  
No. That is for me.

scenes.title: Read Back
paragraphs: *Customs shed, Calder quay · 08:00*

Bram stood between the two men and rendered the answer in the order he had been given it. First the no, in the harbourmaster's own words. Then the doors, each one followed by the plain question: *Have I understood?*

Vey had Bram read the inspector's terms back to him twice. He asked for one change, and Quillan refused it, and Bram carried the refusal exactly, and the captain looked at the table and nodded as at a coin that rang true.

**Vey**  
Brightwater reports to me in writing, signed, and a Concord observer stands on the quay and not on the deck. That much I need for my command.

**Bram**  
The harbourmaster says the inspector signs, the observer stays on the quay.

**Quillan**  
Say that I was never asked whether my harbour wished to be inspected, and that I resent it.

**Bram**  
The harbourmaster says he was never asked whether his harbour wished to be inspected. He resents it. He agrees.

Then Bram read out the ship's conditions as Sefa had asked them to be carried: no names, the sick first, the rifles sealed, the question put to each adult alone. He read them in the order she had spoken them, with the sentence she had added about the vote.

**Vey**  
Rifles. Then I was told the truth.

**Bram**  
The ship's spokeswoman said the same, before anyone asked. She said she would not lie to whoever looked.

**Bram**  
Now the man, Captain. Your paper names Teodor Lask. The ship's answer is this. Brightwater asks every adult aboard, alone, whether they are the man. Each answers for themselves. The answers are written, sealed and held by Brightwater for a hearing on land with counsel. You receive the fact that everyone was asked, and by whom. You do not receive an answer or a name. Have I understood, and can you sign under that?
Vey was quiet long enough that the aide looked up.

**Vey**  
It is not what I was told to bring. I was told to bring a man or a yes. I will not call this a finding. Nobody has told me whether Lask is aboard, and a sealed paper will not tell me either. What I can sign is narrower: that the claim was put to every adult through a neutral, that no ground for custody was established on this quay, and that the allegation is unproved and goes to a hearing with counsel. A refusal I could not sign beneath. That I can.

**Bram**  
You will sign that the question was put to every adult, that the answers are sealed, that you hold no name, and that the allegation is unproved, not answered.

**Vey**  
Unproved. Not disproved. Write it so, because my command will read it both ways. Now my side, and I will say it so your harbourmaster hears it from me and not from a rumour. Two things move me. When the observer on the quay sees the last of the sick landed, and Brightwater sends word in his own hand that he is aboard and the question is being put without obstruction, I go to six kilometres and hold fire. That is mine to do as the officer on station, and it can be undone. If his signed report is not on this table by six this evening, or it says what the observer did not see, I am back at a kilometre and a half by dusk, and I will not send word first.

**Quillan**  
Ask him what six kilometres does for my harbour. I will tell my council what I am given, not what I hope.

**Bram**  
The harbourmaster asks what six kilometres changes for the harbour.

**Vey**  
It opens your harbour mouth. Your pilot boats and your ambulances move without a gun laid on them. My guns still reach this quay from there, and I will not say otherwise. What changes is that I cannot come back to a kilometre and a half unseen. You would watch me close, and that is minutes, not seconds. A harbour can do a great deal with minutes.

**Quillan**  
It is enough.
Vey turned his cap a quarter turn on the table. When he spoke again his voice had changed, and the aide did not write what he said.

**Vey**  
I was sent to collect a handover. This is a better answer than that one, and my command may not think so. Six kilometres. Not away.
Vey stood. At the door he looked at Illuminara for the first time, a man identifying a piece of equipment he had been told nothing about.

**Vey**  
And who are you?

**Bram**  
She is the one who sat behind me.

scenes.title: The Hour After Midnight
paragraphs: *Calder quay · 09:10, and 23:50*

The first stretcher came down the gangway at ten past nine, and the cruiser's rail was lined with men with glasses. The sick went into the ambulances in the order Sefa had set, children first, then the old, then the ones who had walked off on their own and sat down on the cobbles because nobody had told them where to go. Brightwater went up the gangway with a notebook. A Concord observer stood on the quay and watched him do it.

At twenty past eleven the last of the forty-one was in an ambulance, and the observer raised a flag to the cruiser. At ten to twelve a launch brought Brightwater's pencilled note: aboard, rifles sealed and receipted, the question begun in the hold and being put without obstruction. Vey read both on the bridge and logged them. At two in the afternoon the *Marin Resolute* backed out of the harbour mouth and turned side-on, six kilometres out, a grey shape on a grey sea. The harbour mouth lay open for the first time since the blockade began, and a pilot boat went out through it before the cruiser had finished turning. Everyone on the quay knew the guns could still reach them, and nobody pretended otherwise.

Brightwater's signed report reached the customs shed at six. Two crates, sealed, receipts for each. The question put to every adult aboard, each answer or refusal sealed in a case he kept, to be opened at the hearing with counsel or not at all. On the claim about the man he wrote one line, and Vey signed under it: unproved, process followed, no ground for custody established on the quay. Nothing given to Concord. No name recorded. At six the cruiser stayed where it was.
Quillan called Bram to the council hall at eleven. He did not ask him to sit.

**Quillan**  
You carried my no as I gave it. You will not be in my delegation again. I cannot have it said that the harbour's mouth does what it likes.

**Bram**  
Yes, Harbourmaster.
Quillan nodded once, and Bram understood that it was the whole of what was going to be said.

At ten to midnight Bram sat on a bollard at the end of the quay with his coat over his knees. The cruiser's lights burned far out. Illuminara came and sat on the stone beside him, and neither of them spoke while the second hand of the harbour clock crept toward the top of the hour. It passed. Nothing opened fire. A gull moved on a roof.

**Bram**  
He didn't fire.

**Illuminara**  
No.

**Bram**  
I'm out of a job.

**Illuminara**  
You're out of a delegation. Sefa came to the quay at six and asked for you by name. She says the ship has a great deal left to say and nobody on it who can say it to Concord.

Bram looked at the lights six kilometres out, a small steady constellation that would be there in the morning. He did not say anything for a long time. Then he reached down and picked up his satchel and checked, as if it had changed, that his notebook was still inside.

**Bram**  
Tell her I'll be at the gangway at eight.

**Illuminara**  
Tell her yourself. She's still awake.

critic_line: By asking Bram to separate what was said from what he feared—and then refusing to put words in anyone's mouth—Illuminara helps a truthful refusal become medical access, a neutral process, an open harbour mouth and a silent midnight without surrendering a single refugee name.

shared_strengths: A clear, humane premise (an interpreter refuses to soften a word) with dialogue-driven negotiation and a satisfying procedural resolution. The read-back device is memorable. Weaknesses: dense procedural talk in the middle, a passive observer protagonist, and tidy, low-stakes-feeling resolution.

A tense, lucid moral drama turns faithful interpretation into consequential action without making negotiation implausibly easy. Distinct voices, humane constraints, and repeated read-backs build satisfying suspense; only the procedural denouement slightly slows the momentum. The quiet final exchange gives Bram’s costly integrity an earned future.
shared_reservations: The ship was a coastal packet built for ninety and carrying two hundred and twelve. Sefa Harrow, a retired schoolteacher with a blanket over her shoulders and a clipboard she no longer needed, met Illuminara
At twenty past eleven the last of the forty-one was in an ambulance, and the observer raised a flag to the cruiser.

translation_sl.title: TOLMAČ, KI SO GA PROSILI, NAJ OMEHČA BESEDO
translation_sl.deck: Kapitan, ki blokira pristanišče, pravi, da bo morda razumel kot da. Devetnajstletnemu tolmaču pristaniškega mojstra ukažejo, naj odločno zavrnitev prevede kot »o tem razmišljamo«. Illuminara za mizo nima nobenega položaja, zato sede za njim in počaka, da ji zastavi vprašanje.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov skozi eno noč in naslednji dan: ukaz, naj se beseda omehča; miza, pri kateri je natančna zavrnitev izrečena in ponovljena; pomol, kjer ladja pove, kaj bo dovolila in kako se sme vprašati človeka; pristaniški mojster, ki mora vsako popuščanje izreči na glas; jutro ponavljanj in postopnega, povratnega zaupanja; ter ura po tem, ko rok mine v tišini.

scenes.title: Dve besedi in še tri
paragraphs: *Dvorana sveta, pristanišče Calder · petindvajset ur pred iztekom roka, 22.40*
Pristaniški mojster Calderja je svoj odgovor napisal na hrbtno stran tablice plimovanja, dolg pa je bil dve besedi.

Quillan Abara jo je položil pred Brama Ivarssona. Bram je imel devetnajst let. Tolmačil je za ribiške žene in carinske uradnike, nikoli pa za kogar koli z orožjem. Illuminara je sedela na zložljivem stolu ob steni, kamor jo je postavil svet, ker nihče ni znal reči, kaj drugega bi lahko bila. Skozi okno je križarka *Marin Resolute* ležala čez pristaniško ustje kakor zaprta vrata, z vsemi prižganimi palubnimi lučmi.

**Quillan**  
Preberi.

**Bram**  
Ne. Ladje *Tamsin Reach* ne bomo predali.

**Quillan**  
To je moj odgovor in pravilen je. Zdaj pa poslušaj, kaj boš rekel za mizo.
Vzel je tablico plimovanja nazaj in pod prvi dve besedi napisal še tri, tako močno, da je v papir vtisnil vdolbino.

**Quillan**  
*O tem razmišljamo.* Kapitan, ki sliši, da razmišljamo, počaka. Kapitan, ki sliši ne, strelja. Kapitan Vey nam je povedal, kako sliši stvari, jaz pa bi raje ostal neslišan.

**Bram**  
Rekel je, da bo morda vzel kot da.

**Quillan**  
Potem bom imel eno noč, preden bo kdo ugotovil, da ni bilo tako. Šestdeset tisoč ljudi potrebuje eno noč, fant. Preneseš, kar ti je dano. To je vse tvoje delo.

Bram je pogledal dve besedi in tri. Dobro si je zapomnil, kar so ljudje rekli, in to je bilo edino, za kar je zanesljivo vedel, da mu gre. *Če prenesem te tri, sem laž položil v lastna usta in ji rekel usluga.*

**Bram**  
Prenesel bom ne, pristaniški mojster. Ne vem, ali lahko prenesem tisto drugo.

Quillan ni odgovoril. Obrnil se je k oknu in obstal z rokami za hrbtom kakor človek, ki čaka na kazen, ki jo je že prestal. Illuminara ni rekla ničesar. V tej sobi ni imela nobenega položaja in začela je misliti, da je najprijaznejše, kar lahko postane, stol, ki se ne nagiba.

scenes.title: Kaj bi slišal kapitan
paragraphs: *Carinska lopa, pomol v Calderju · 23.30*

Kapitan Anselm Vey je bil negiben kakor človek, ki dva dni ni spal in tega ni nameraval omeniti. Na kopno je prišel v čolnu s križarke z enim pomočnikom, ki je pisal in nikoli spregovoril, nato pa sedel na drugo stran carinske mize, s čepico poravnano pred seboj.

**Vey**  
Pristaniški mojster. Imeli ste večer. Kakšen je vaš odgovor?
Quillan je v pristaniškem jeziku izrekel štiri kratke besede. Bram se je obrnil h kapitanu. Glas je zvenel tiše, kakor si je želel, in pustil ga je takega.

**Bram**  
Pristaniški mojster pravi ne. Ladje ne bomo predali.
Pomočnikovo pero se je ustavilo. Vey je dolgo gledal Brama, Illuminara pa je s stola ob vratih videla, kako je kapitan dojel, da mladenič ni rekel *razmišljamo*.

**Vey**  
Potem vam bom povedal, kako to slišim. Jutri opolnoči bodo moji topovi odprli ogenj na ta pomol. Nič, kar bo izrečeno po nocojšnjem večeru, ne bo doseglo nikogar, ki jih lahko ustavi.

Bram je prevedel. Quillanova čeljust se je premaknila. Bram je začutil, kako se soba nagiba k edini stvari, za katero mu nihče ni povedal, da jo sme storiti, in prosil za vodo. Na hodniku se je naslonil na steno, Illuminara pa je prišla ven in obstala tako daleč, da bi razdaljo lahko zmanjšal ali pa ne.

**Bram**  
Naredil sem prav. Povedal sem natančno, pa bo streljal. Poslabšal sem stvari.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj je rekel, da bo storil? Ne kaj si slišal. Kaj je rekel.

**Bram**  
Jutri opolnoči bo odprl ogenj. Nič, kar bo izrečeno po nocojšnjem večeru, ne bo doseglo nikogar, ki ga lahko ustavi.

**Illuminara**  
To sta datum in strah. Ne pove, kaj bi to spremenilo. Kaj bi želel vedeti, če bi moral prav ti to odnesti nazaj poveljstvu?
Strmel je vanjo. Nato se je počasi nekaj v njegovem obrazu nehalo upirati in začelo delati.

**Bram**  
Dovoljeno mi je ponoviti. Preden odgovorim, lahko ponovim vse, kar mislim, da sem slišal. Nihče me še nikoli ni prosil, naj to uporabim pri kapitanu.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom ti povedala, kaj vprašati. Tukaj bom.
Ko se je vrnil, ni sedel. Najprej je povedal v marinščini, nato v pristaniškem jeziku, počasi, da bi oba moža slišala, kaj je razumel.

**Bram**  
Kapitan, ponovil bom, kar sem slišal, vi pa mi boste povedali, kje se motim. Jutri opolnoči boste streljali. Razumel sem, da boste streljali, če ne dobite privolitve. Ali to mislite, ali pa mislite, da boste streljali, če ne dobite nečesa, o čemer lahko poročate?
Vey več vdihov ni rekel ničesar. Njegov pomočnik je spet začel pisati.

**Vey**  
Ne privolitve. Ne potrebujem vaše ladje. Mojemu poveljstvu so povedali, da so na njej orožje in en človek, ki ga hočejo. Ukazano mi je streljati, če ne dobim odgovora na to trditev, ki ga lahko preverim. Privolitev je preverljiva. Morda ni. Tudi ne, za katerim ni ničesar, ni.

**Bram**  
To sta dve trditvi, kapitan, in pristaniški mojster bo nanju odgovoril ločeno. Orožje in človek. Kakšna je trditev o človeku?

**Vey**  
Nalog vzhodnega sodišča Concorda. Teodor Lask, obtožen požiga žitnega skladišča pri Orrin Fordu. Razen papirja nimam nobenega dokaza. Ne vem, ali je na krovu. Moje poveljstvo pravi, da je. Nisem sodišče in tudi vas ne prosim, da bi bili.

**Bram**  
Kaj pa bi sprejeli kot odgovor o njem?

**Vey**  
Da bi pogledal nekdo, ki ne odgovarja nobeni mornarici, zapisal, kaj je našel, jaz pa bi se lahko podpisal pod njegov zapis. Pod zavrnitev se ne morem podpisati.
Bram je Quillanu prevedel vse, vsako besedo, in opazoval pristaniškega mojstra, kako je prvič slišal, iz česa so bila narejena vrata.

**Bram**  
Pristaniški mojster, kapitan lahko živi z ne, če ga spremlja način, kako odgovoriti na njegovo trditev. Jaz ga ne morem ponuditi. Tolmač ne dodaja.

**Quillan**  
Na krovu beguncev ne bom dovolil škornjev Concorda. In človeka ne bom predal zaradi kapitanovega papirja.

**Bram**  
To sta dve zavrnitvi. Ne vem še, kaj drugega lahko odprete vi.

**Quillan**  
Ne za mizo. Ne pod topovi. Odgovoril bom ob štirih.
Vey je to dovolil. Njegov pomočnik je pod stranjo potegnil črto.

scenes.title: Kaj bi dovolila ladja
paragraphs: *Pomol, ob ladji Tamsin Reach · 01.20*

Ladja je bila obalni paketnik, zgrajen za devetdeset ljudi, na njej pa jih je bilo dvesto dvanajst. Sefa Harrow, upokojena učiteljica z odejo čez ramena in pisalno podlogo, ki je ni več potrebovala, je Illuminari prišla naproti ob vznožju mostička in ji ni ponudila roke.

**Sefa**  
Nocoj hočejo vsi govoriti v našem imenu. Pristaniški mojster, kapitan, radio. Ti si prva, ki je prišla sem dol vprašat.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem še vprašala. Prišla sem vprašat, česa ne bi nikoli dovolili. Potem pa, kaj bi lahko.

**Sefa**  
Imena. Seznam dvesto dvanajstih imen v pisarni Concorda pomeni dvesto dvanajst ljudi, ki jih lahko najdejo. Niti eno ime ne zapusti te ladje.

**Illuminara**  
Potem brez imen. Kaj še?

**Sefa**  
Enainštirideset mojih je bolnih. Nekateri so bolni že en teden. Kar koli želi kdor koli videti v mojem podpalubju, naj najprej vidi bolne oditi z ladje.
Nekje nad njima je zakašljal otrok, trdo in mokro. Sefa je počakala, da je kašelj minil.

**Sefa**  
In to moraš slišati od mene, preden slišiš od kapitana. V podpalubju sta dva zaboja lovskih pušk. Dve družini sta jih iz navade prinesli z obale. Ne moti se povsem in nikomur, kogar pošljete, ne bom lagala.

**Illuminara**  
Potem to sama poveš tistemu, ki bo pogledal. Ne bom govorila namesto tebe. V njegovi trditvi je še nekaj in ni tovor. Človek. Hočeš ime ali samo podatek, da nekdo je?

**Sefa**  
Povej. Slišati ne pomeni predati.

**Illuminara**  
Teodor Lask. Nalog vzhodnega sodišča zaradi požiga žitnega skladišča pri Orrin Fordu. Kapitan pravi, da ne ve, ali je človek na krovu.
Sefin obraz se ni spremenil. Nekje nad njima je prenehal kašelj ali pa dih. Illuminara ne bi mogla reči, kaj, in ni pogledala navzgor.

**Sefa**  
Ne bom ti povedala, ali poznam to ime. Če rečem ne, kapitanu dolgujem dokaz za ne. Če rečem da, sem mu izročila človeka, ker mi je mornarica položila pred oči papir. Noben od teh odgovorov ne zapusti ladje.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa jo lahko?

**Sefa**  
Glasovanje ne more predati človeka. Odloči lahko samo, kako ga bodo vprašali. Torej: nekdo, ki ne odgovarja nobeni mornarici, vsakemu odraslemu na krovu na samem postavi eno vprašanje. Ste vi človek na tem papirju? Vsak odgovori zase in nihče za nikogar drugega. Odgovor se zapiše, zapečati in ga ta nevtralna oseba hrani do obravnave na kopnem, z zagovornikom za tistega, na kogar se nanaša. Kapitan lahko dobi podatek, da je bilo vprašanje postavljeno vsem nam. Odgovora ne sme dobiti.

**Illuminara**  
Prenesla bom natanko to in ničesar poleg.

**Sefa**  
Glasujemo ob treh. Z dvigom rok, v podpalubju, vsi, starejši od dvanajst let. Ob štirih ti povem, kaj pravi ladja.

Deset minut pred četrto je sama prišla do mostička. Ladja je glasovala. Puške bodo zapečatene in v hrambi nevtralnega inšpektorja, dokler pristanišče ne bo varno. Bolni bodo odšli prvi. Vsakega odraslega bodo vprašali na samem in noben odgovor ne bo zapustil ladje. Nobeno ime ne bo zapustilo ladje. En moški je glasoval proti in ni govoril z nikomer; Sefa je to povedala brez opravičila.

scenes.title: Povej na glas
paragraphs: *Dvorana sveta, pristanišče Calder · 04.20*
Quillan je bil še vedno v plašču. Bram je prinesel čaj in ga odložil brez zahvale, nato pa storil nekaj, kar ga je nekaj stalo: ni sedel.

**Bram**  
Pristaniški mojster, ob osmih bom vaš ne prenesel natanko tako, kot ste mi ga dali. Ne bom rekel, da razmišljamo. Če mi to ukažete, vam zdaj povem, da ne bom, vi pa lahko pošljete po koga drugega.

**Quillan**  
Devetnajst let imaš.

**Bram**  
Da. Kapitan bo opolnoči streljal na ne, za katerim ni ničesar. Ne bom usta, ki pravijo, da ste razmišljali, ko niste. Povejte mi, kaj je vaše, da odprete. Vsako stvar izrecite na glas in jaz vam jo bom ponovil, nato pa bom prenesel natanko to in nič več.
Illuminara je stala ob vratih. Sefa jo je prosila, naj mu prinese štiri ladijske pogoje, in to je ob štirih v dvorani storila, besedo za besedo. Zdaj ni dodala ničesar.

**Quillan**  
Nevtralen inšpektor. Ne človek Concorda. Tomas Brightwater iz Misije svetilke čaka v mestu že od prvega dne.

**Bram**  
Nevtralen inšpektor, Brightwater iz Misije svetilke, ne častnik Concorda. Je to vaše, da ponudite?

**Quillan**  
Je. Bolni prvi, ob devetih, na moj pomol, v moja reševalna vozila. In če se topovi odmaknejo, pogovor naslednji dan ob zori.

**Bram**  
Bolni se ob devetih izkrcajo v vaša reševalna vozila. Če se topovi odmaknejo, pogovor naslednji dan ob zori. Je to vaše, da ponudite?

**Quillan**  
Je. In četrti pogoj ladje, vprašanje vsakemu odraslemu na samem. Moje pristanišče Brightwaterju dovoljuje, da ga zastavi na mojem pomolu in v njihovem podpalubju. Odgovori so njihovi. Ne bom dopustil, da se sliši, kot da mornarici obljubljam nekaj, česar ne morem obljubiti.

**Bram**  
Pristanišče dovoljuje, da se vprašanje zastavi. Odgovori pripadajo ladji. Je to tisto, kar dajete?

**Quillan**  
Natanko to dajem. In poslušaj še to, ker ne bom dovolil, da bi pozneje rekli, da sem to izbral z veseljem. To počnem, ker neki fant ni hotel lagati zame.

**Bram**  
Tudi to lahko prevedem, če želite.

**Quillan**  
Ne. To je zame.

scenes.title: Ponovi
paragraphs: *Carinska lopa, pomol v Calderju · 08.00*

Bram je stal med možema in odgovor prevedel v vrstnem redu, v katerem mu je bil dan. Najprej ne, z lastnimi besedami pristaniškega mojstra. Nato odprta vrata, za vsakimi pa jasno vprašanje: *Sem prav razumel?*

Vey je od Brama zahteval, naj mu inšpektorjeve pogoje dvakrat ponovi. Prosil je za eno spremembo, Quillan jo je zavrnil, Bram pa je zavrnitev prenesel natančno; kapitan je pogledal mizo in prikimal kakor ob kovancu, ki čisto zazveni.

**Vey**  
Brightwater mi poroča pisno in podpisano, opazovalec Concorda pa stoji na pomolu in ne na palubi. Toliko potrebujem za svoje poveljstvo.

**Bram**  
Pristaniški mojster pravi, da se inšpektor podpiše, opazovalec pa ostane na pomolu.

**Quillan**  
Povej, da me nihče ni vprašal, ali moje pristanišče želi biti pregledano, in da mi to ni všeč.

**Bram**  
Pristaniški mojster pravi, da ga nihče ni vprašal, ali njegovo pristanišče želi biti pregledano. Temu nasprotuje. Strinja se.

Nato je Bram prebral ladijske pogoje, kakor je Sefa prosila, naj jih prenese: brez imen, bolni prvi, puške zapečatene, vprašanje vsakemu odraslemu na samem. Prebral jih je v vrstnem redu, v katerem jih je izrekla, skupaj s stavkom, ki ga je dodala o glasovanju.

**Vey**  
Puške. Potem so mi povedali resnico.

**Bram**  
Predstavnica ladje je isto povedala, še preden je kdo vprašal. Rekla je, da ne bo lagala tistemu, ki bo pogledal.

**Bram**  
Zdaj človek, kapitan. Na vašem papirju piše Teodor Lask. Odgovor ladje je takšen. Brightwater vsakega odraslega na krovu na samem vpraša, ali je ta človek. Vsak odgovori zase. Odgovori so zapisani, zapečateni in jih Brightwater hrani za obravnavo na kopnem z zagovornikom. Vi prejmete podatek, da so bili vprašani vsi, in kdo jih je vprašal. Ne prejmete odgovora ali imena. Sem prav razumel in ali se lahko pod to podpišete?
Vey je molčal tako dolgo, da je pomočnik pogledal navzgor.

**Vey**  
To ni tisto, kar so mi naročili prinesti. Naročili so mi, naj pripeljem človeka ali privolitev. Tega ne bom imenoval ugotovitev. Nihče mi ni povedal, ali je Lask na krovu, in tudi zapečaten papir mi ne bo. Podpišem lahko nekaj ožjega: da je bila trditev prek nevtralne osebe predložena vsakemu odraslemu, da na tem pomolu ni bila ugotovljena podlaga za pridržanje ter da trditev ni dokazana in gre v obravnavo z zagovornikom. Pod zavrnitev se ne bi mogel podpisati. Pod to se lahko.

**Bram**  
Podpisali boste, da je bilo vprašanje postavljeno vsakemu odraslemu, da so odgovori zapečateni, da nimate nobenega imena in da trditev ni dokazana, ne pa odgovorjena.

**Vey**  
Ni dokazana. Ni ovržena. Tako napišite, ker bo moje poveljstvo to bralo na oba načina. Zdaj pa moja stran; povedal jo bom tako, da jo vaš pristaniški mojster sliši od mene in ne iz govoric. Dve stvari me premakneta. Ko opazovalec na pomolu vidi, da se je izkrcal zadnji bolnik, in Brightwater lastnoročno pošlje sporočilo, da je na krovu in da vprašanje postavljajo brez oviranja, se umaknem na šest kilometrov in zadržim ogenj. Kot častnik na položaju imam pravico to storiti in odločitev je mogoče razveljaviti. Če njegovo podpisano poročilo ne bo na tej mizi do šestih zvečer ali če bo pisalo kaj drugega od tistega, kar je videl opazovalec, bom do mraka spet na kilometru in pol in prej ne bom poslal obvestila.

**Quillan**  
Vprašaj ga, kaj šest kilometrov pomeni za moje pristanišče. Svojemu svetu bom povedal, kaj dobim, ne česa upam.

**Bram**  
Pristaniški mojster sprašuje, kaj šest kilometrov spremeni za pristanišče.

**Vey**  
Odpre vaše pristaniško ustje. Vaši pilotski čolni in reševalna vozila se premikajo, ne da bi bili topovi uperjeni vanje. Moji topovi od tam še vedno dosežejo ta pomol in ne bom trdil drugače. Spremeni se to, da se ne morem neopaženo vrniti na kilometer in pol. Opazovali bi me, kako se približujem, in to so minute, ne sekunde. Pristanišče lahko z minutami stori veliko.

**Quillan**  
Dovolj je.
Vey je čepico na mizi obrnil za četrt obrata. Ko je znova spregovoril, se je njegov glas spremenil, pomočnik pa ni zapisal njegovih besed.

**Vey**  
Poslali so me po predajo. To je boljši odgovor od tistega, moje poveljstvo pa morda ne bo tako mislilo. Šest kilometrov. Ne odhod.
Vey je vstal. Pri vratih je prvič pogledal Illuminaro kakor človek, ki prepoznava kos opreme, o katerem mu niso ničesar povedali.

**Vey**  
In kdo ste vi?

**Bram**  
Ona je tista, ki je sedela za menoj.

scenes.title: Ura po polnoči
paragraphs: *Pomol v Calderju · 09.10 in 23.50*

Prva nosila so prišla po mostičku navzdol deset minut čez deveto, ograja križarke pa je bila obdana z možmi z daljnogledi. Bolni so odšli v reševalna vozila v vrstnem redu, ki ga je določila Sefa: najprej otroci, nato stari, potem tisti, ki so z ladje odšli sami in sedli na tlakovce, ker jim nihče ni povedal, kam naj gredo. Brightwater se je z beležnico povzpel po mostičku. Opazovalec Concorda je stal na pomolu in gledal, kako je to storil.

Dvajset minut čez enajsto je bil zadnji od enainštiridesetih v reševalnem vozilu, opazovalec pa je proti križarki dvignil zastavo. Deset minut pred poldnevom je čoln prinesel Brightwaterjevo s svinčnikom napisano sporočilo: na krovu, puške zapečatene in potrjene s potrdili, spraševanje se je začelo v podpalubju in poteka brez oviranja. Vey je na mostu prebral oboje in vpisal v dnevnik. Ob dveh popoldne se je *Marin Resolute* umaknila iz pristaniškega ustja in se šest kilometrov proč obrnila z bokom, siva oblika na sivem morju. Pristaniško ustje je bilo prvič od začetka blokade odprto, pilotski čoln pa je zapeljal skozenj, še preden se je križarka nehala obračati. Vsi na pomolu so vedeli, da jih topovi še vedno lahko dosežejo, in nihče se ni pretvarjal drugače.

Brightwaterjevo podpisano poročilo je ob šestih prispelo v carinsko lopo. Dva zaboja, zapečatena, za vsakega potrdilo. Vprašanje je bilo postavljeno vsakemu odraslemu na krovu, vsak odgovor ali zavrnitev pa zapečatena v zabojčku, ki ga je hranil in bi ga odprli na obravnavi z zagovornikom ali pa sploh ne. O trditvi glede človeka je napisal eno vrstico, Vey pa se je podpisal pod njo: ni dokazano, postopek izveden, na pomolu ni bila ugotovljena podlaga za pridržanje. Concord ni dobil ničesar. Zapisano ni bilo nobeno ime. Ob šestih je križarka ostala, kjer je bila.
Quillan je ob enajstih poklical Brama v dvorano sveta. Ni mu rekel, naj sede.

**Quillan**  
Moj ne si prenesel tako, kot sem ti ga dal. V moji delegaciji te ne bo več. Ne morem dovoliti, da bi se govorilo, da usta pristanišča počnejo, kar se jim zljubi.

**Bram**  
Da, pristaniški mojster.
Quillan je enkrat prikimal in Bram je razumel, da je to vse, kar bo izrečeno.

Deset minut pred polnočjo je Bram sedel na priveznem stebričku na koncu pomola, s plaščem čez kolena. Luči križarke so gorele daleč na morju. Illuminara je prišla in sedla na kamen ob njem; nobeden ni spregovoril, medtem ko se je sekundni kazalec pristaniške ure plazil proti vrhu ure. Šel je čez. Nič ni odprlo ognja. Na strehi se je premaknil galeb.

**Bram**  
Ni streljal.

**Illuminara**  
Ne.

**Bram**  
Brez službe sem.

**Illuminara**  
Izpadel si iz delegacije. Sefa je ob šestih prišla na pomol in vprašala po tebi z imenom. Pravi, da ima ladja še veliko povedati, na njej pa ni nikogar, ki bi to lahko povedal Concordu.

Bram je pogledal luči šest kilometrov proč, majhno mirno ozvezdje, ki bo zjutraj še vedno tam. Dolgo ni rekel ničesar. Nato je segel navzdol, pobral torbo in preveril, kakor da bi se lahko spremenilo, ali je beležnica še vedno v njej.

**Bram**  
Povej ji, da bom ob osmih pri mostičku.

**Illuminara**  
Povej ji sam. Še vedno je budna.

translation_sl.critic_line: Ko Illuminara Brama prosi, naj loči izrečeno od tistega, česar se boji — in nato noče nikomur polagati besed v usta — pomaga, da resnična zavrnitev postane zdravstveni dostop, nevtralen postopek, odprto pristaniško ustje in tiha polnoč, ne da bi predala eno samo ime begunca.
